doc.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Great musicians of every race in jazz
summary: Benson says Art Blakey corrected Miles's remarks and argues jazz was built by musicians of all races.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: others. There are great musicians of all races in jazz music. I know, because I played with them.
You can talk about it back in Pittsburgh, all the cats back there.

Later I played with the greatest. Some of them happened to be Caucasians. I played with some Mexican musicians, Cuban musicians, Puerto Rican musicians, everywhere, European guys. So I know the difference. When Art Blakey said that, he straightened me out, because in my mind, I couldn’t get past the Miles Davis statement that he made in the studio years ago. It’s all done now. Teo Macero knew it. I wish I had talked to him. What’s you got?
